# How the GitHub contribution calendar works

This guide gathers what three investigations learned about the calendar while fixing `lookup` and `suggest` ([MAIN-159](../issues/MAIN-159.md)). It covers what GitHub documents, what we measured, what stays unexplained and how maintainer uses it. Every claim names its source. `[S…]` refers to the [Sources](#sources), and "measured" means a live request made by one of the investigations on the date given.

**Slice.** `main` at `c1bf934`, with the uncommitted MAIN-159 change in the working copy. Account `kamilsk`, classic personal access token with `repo` scope, in `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The owner and the Mac moved from Europe/Moscow to Asia/Tokyo in late October 2026. The measurements were taken on 2026-10-03, 2026-10-30 and 2026-10-31.

## In short

- There are two views of one calendar. The **public profile** (`/users/<login>/contributions`) puts a pull request review on its **UTC** date. The **GraphQL** `contributionCalendar` puts it on the date in the **request's time zone**: the `Time-Zone` header when GitHub honours it, otherwise the user's last known zone, which follows the browser. Both views count the same events, so the totals agree while the days differ.
- When the account's zone changes, GraphQL **re-buckets the whole history**. On 2026-10-03, with the account in Moscow, 2024 and 2025 matched the profile. After the move to Tokyo, 160 days of 2025 differ.
- Commits, issues and pull requests sit on the same dates in both views. GraphQL also moves a created repository by the request's zone [Codex].
- `from`/`to` of a collection select **whole days in the request's zone**, the days of the UTC dates of `from` and `to`. A review at 20:00Z on December 31 belongs to the next year's collection when the zone is Tokyo.
- A collection counts **one review per pull request, the latest**. A year therefore counts fewer reviews than the sum of its months.
- Some contributions have **no events** in the API, such as ones in private repositories the token cannot read (`restrictedContributionsCount`). Only the calendar knows their days.
- Rebuilding the days from the GraphQL events by the profile's rules reproduces the profile **exactly** for kamilsk in 2013, 2024, 2025 and 2026. maintainer does this since MAIN-159 and caches the events by month.
- The API cannot read the account's zone. The `Time-Zone` header changes the placement, but in the Codex investigation identical requests alternated between the two variants. Only the HTML is an exact copy of the profile; GitHub does not document it, and the owner rejected it as the main source.

## The two views

### Profile HTML

- `https://github.com/users/<login>/contributions?from=YYYY-01-01&to=YYYY-12-31` returns the calendar fragment of a year without authentication [measured 2026-10-30, 2026-10-31].
- A day is a `<td … data-date="2025-01-03" id="contribution-day-component-<weekday>-<week>" data-level="…">`. Its count is in the tooltip bound by id: `<tool-tip … for="contribution-day-component-…">15 contributions on January 3rd.</tool-tip>`, or `No contributions on …` [measured]. grubersjoe/github-contributions-api parses the same markup [S10].
- Reviews are on their UTC date. Commits are on their own date: a commit at 00:26+03:00 was not moved to the previous UTC day [measured 2026-10-03].
- The `tz` cookie changes nothing. Without it and with UTC, Moscow, Tokyo or Los Angeles, the 365 cells of 2025 are the same [measured 2026-10-03; Codex].
- **The logged-in profile shows the same as the anonymous one.** The owner checked January 3–5, 2025 in the browser and saw 15, 15, 15 [Codex, owner's answer 2026-10-30]. Other dates were not checked that way.
- Three reads of 2026 gave the same 303 days and 6901 contributions [Codex 2026-10-30].
- Private contributions are visible only as anonymized counts, and only if the profile setting is on [S1]. kamilsk has it on: the HTML total of 2023 is above the API one.
- The year-scoped profile tab, `https://github.com/<login>?tab=contributions&from=<year>-01-01`, is a different endpoint. It is served from caches of different ages: six requests gave three values for the day still being indexed. It needs `X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest`, otherwise the response has an `include-fragment` placeholder instead of the calendar. `cache-control` headers and unique query parameters do not stabilise it. `?tab=contributions` without a year and `/users/<login>/contributions` answered consistently in 8 of 8 requests ([MAIN-126](../issues/MAIN-126.md), issue #457).
- grubersjoe/github-contributions-api requests a year as `/users/<u>/contributions?tab=overview&from=<year>-12-01&to=<year>-12-31` [S10]. We did not test that form.

### GraphQL

- `user(login:).contributionsCollection(from:, to:)` or `viewer.contributionsCollection`. The arguments are only `organizationID`, `from` and `to`, and `contributionCalendar` takes none [Codex: live schema; S8]. A collection spans at most one year ([MAIN-126](../issues/MAIN-126.md)). A token is required even for a public profile.
- `contributionCalendar { totalContributions weeks { contributionDays { date contributionCount } } }` returns the days of the range, already bucketed.
- `user(login)`, `viewer` and `node(id)` give the same variant within one response [Codex].
- The placement follows the **requesting** account, not the profile owner. Read with kamilsk's token, the calendars of thockin and BurntSushi have their reviews in Tokyo. For thockin, reviews in Tokyo plus issues and PRs in Los Angeles match all 88 days of July–September 2025, and reviews in any other zone are off on at least 49 days [research run 2026-10-31].

### Other sources

- The REST events API returns at most 300 events of the past 30 days [S7]. It is no source for a calendar.
- Established tools either parse the HTML (grubersjoe/github-contributions-api [S10], sallar/github-contributions-api [S11]) or read `contributionCalendar` with the deployer's token (github-readme-streak-stats [S12], github-profile-3d-contrib on `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` [S13]). github-readme-stats reads totals only [S14]. None of them mentions the review shift. A maintainer of streak-stats wrote in #900: "there does not appear to be a way to change the timezone in the GitHub GraphQL API" [S12, quoted by the research run].

## What counts

From the reference [S2] and troubleshooting [S5]:

- **Always counted:** creating a repository and forking one.
- **Sometimes counted:** opening an issue, proposing a pull request, submitting a review, opening or answering a discussion, and making a commit.
- **Issues, PRs and discussions** count only in a standalone repository, not a fork. "GitHub limits the number of these items when displaying the contribution graph."
- **Commits** count when all three hold: the author email is on the account, the repository is not a fork, and the branch is the default one or `gh-pages`. In addition, at least one of these holds: you are a collaborator or org member, you forked the repository, or you opened an issue or PR in it.
- **The author date** places a commit on the profile; in a repository, the commit date is used.
- A new contribution may take **up to 24 hours** to appear, and so may a graph rebuild.
- Activity of an SAML SSO organization is hidden without an active SSO session. Outsiders see it anonymized [S1].
- GitHub Enterprise Server shares counts of the last 90 days. GitHub Connect updates them hourly, and they count as private [S2].
- The UI lets you select at most a one-month range of the calendar [S6].

## Time zones

### What GitHub documents

- "Contributions are timestamped according to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) rather than your local time zone" [S1]. The profile follows this; GraphQL does not, for reviews.
- "**Commits** use the time zone information in the commit timestamp. **Pull requests** and **issues** opened on GitHub use your browser's time zone. Those opened via the API use the timestamp or time zone specified in the API call" [S2, S9].
- The REST API picks a zone in this order: an explicit offset in the timestamp, then the `Time-Zone` header (an Olson name), then the authenticated user's last known zone, then UTC. "The last known timezone is updated whenever you browse the GitHub website." GitHub says these rules apply to data passed to the API, not to data it returns [S3]. They describe what we see in the GraphQL calendar, but GitHub does not document that.
- The profile can display the local time, with a Time zone menu in its settings [S4]. That setting is display-only, and nothing ties it to the calendar.
- GitHub's public JavaScript reads `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone` and writes the `tz` cookie [Codex, from `behaviors-*.js`].

### What we measured, by contribution type

| Contribution | Profile HTML | GraphQL calendar | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PR review | UTC date of `occurredAt` | Date in the request's zone | Events by UTC = profile, events by Tokyo = GraphQL: 0 differing days in 2024 and 2025 [measured 2026-10-31] |
| Commit | Date of the author timestamp in its own offset | Same | 0 differing days in 2024–2026; `occurredAt` of a commit day is 07:00Z/08:00Z, midnight in Los Angeles (2025: 260 and 252 nodes) [measured] |
| Issue, pull request | Date at creation: browser zone on the web, UTC through the API | Same | 2022 matches better with Moscow than with UTC (5 against 17 differing days); 2026 matches by UTC [measured], probably because the owner's mirror opens issues through the API [research run] |
| Created repository | UTC date | Request's zone | `2026-05-21T16:36:21Z` is May 22 in GraphQL and May 21 in HTML [Codex] |
| Restricted (no access for the token) | Anonymized count on its day | Count on its day | No events in the API; see [Contributions without events](#contributions-without-events) |

- **History moves with the zone.** On 2026-10-03 (Moscow), GraphQL and the profile differed only on 18 days in 2022–2023: reviews between 00:00 and 03:00 MSK. 2024–2025 had none [measured 2026-10-03]. On 2026-10-30 (Tokyo), 2025 differs on 160 days with the same total, 6141 [Codex; measured 2026-10-31].
- **Example.** On January 3, 2025, 15 reviews were made at 20:06–20:19Z, which is already January 4 in Tokyo. GraphQL shows 0 / 22 / 23 for January 3–5, the profile 15 / 15 / 15 [measured].
- **maintainer's Go client sends no `Time-Zone`,** so GitHub falls back to the last known zone, and `TZ` of the process changes nothing. Its output was the same with `TZ=Europe/Moscow` and `TZ=Asia/Tokyo` [Codex].
- **`gh api` sends `Time-Zone: <local zone>` itself:** `gh api --verbose` shows `> Time-Zone: Asia/Tokyo` [measured 2026-10-31]. Compare `gh` and Go requests only after checking the headers [Codex].
- **The `Time-Zone` header is not ignored, but it is unreliable.**
  - For January 11 – December 17, 2025, the sequence UTC / Tokyo / UTC gave 0 / 153 / 0 days off the HTML [Codex].
  - Six identical requests on one connection (`Time-Zone: UTC`, 2026-10-30 12:55Z) gave the following counts for January 3, 2025. Each yearly calendar was one of two variants: the HTML exactly, or 160 days off.

    | `X-GitHub-Request-Id` | Year range | One-day range |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `D7C4:1D6068:30CBF2:46B827:6AE493B2` | 15 | 0 |
    | `D7C4:1D6068:30E150:46D83C:6AE493B4` | 0 | 15 |
    | `D7C4:1D6068:30EA45:46E588:6AE493B5` | 0 | 0 |
    | `D7C4:1D6068:30F4F1:46F55F:6AE493B6` | 0 | 0 |
    | `D7C4:1D6068:30FF91:47044B:6AE493B7` | 15 | 15 |
    | `D7C4:1D6068:3110B4:471DB4:6AE493B8` | 0 | 0 |

  - About ten hours later, nine requests with UTC gave 15 / 15. Three requests without the header gave 0/15, 0/15 and 15/15 [Codex].
  - On 2026-10-31, five requests each without the header, with UTC and with Tokyo were stable. UTC moved 5 reviews of `2026-04-30T19:21Z` from the May collection into the April one (April 450 / May 500 with UTC, 445 / 505 otherwise) [measured].
- **The account's zone cannot be read.** Introspection of the GraphQL schema finds no timezone, utcOffset or localTime field, and REST `/user` has none either. The anonymous profile has no `profile-timezone` element unless the owner displays the local time [research run 2026-10-31].
- **Unverified idea:** a token without a user zone (a GitHub App installation token, the Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN`) might get the UTC calendar in one request. It would take one `workflow_dispatch` run in a scratch repository to settle. GitHub may also default to Pacific time: the commit days come as 07:00Z/08:00Z [research run].

## How `from` and `to` select events

The range covers **whole days in the request's zone: the days whose dates `from` and `to` have in UTC**. Neither the time of day nor the offset written in the argument matters [measured 2026-10-31, through `gh` with the Tokyo header; maintainer's Go client without a header met the same boundary].

| `from` .. `to` | Reviews | First / last `occurredAt` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `2023-03-01T00:00:00Z .. 2023-03-31T23:59:59Z` | 235 | `2023-02-28T15:32:32Z` / `2023-03-31T07:07:01Z` |
| `2023-03-01T00:00:00+09:00 .. 2023-03-31T23:59:59+09:00` | 235 | same |
| `2023-02-28T15:00:00Z .. 2023-03-31T14:59:59Z` | 235 | same |
| `2023-03-01T12:00:00Z .. 2023-03-31T12:00:00Z` | 235 | same |
| `2026-04-30T00:00:00Z .. 2026-04-30T19:30:00Z` | 7 | excludes `2026-04-30T19:21Z` (May 1 in Tokyo) |
| `2026-04-30T00:00:00Z .. 2026-05-01T00:00:00Z` | 12 | includes it |

- `startedAt` and `endedAt` echo the arguments, not the window that was used [measured].
- Collections of consecutive UTC months do not overlap: they are consecutive local months.
- An event of a UTC year can sit in the collection of the day next to it: December 31 after 15:00Z is in next year's January in Tokyo. For a zone west of UTC, January 1 before the offset is in last year's December.

## One review per pull request

- A collection lists, and the calendar counts, **one review per pull request: the latest one in its range**. The live schema describes this choice [Codex].
- The yearly lists of 2023, 2024 and 2025 have 3, 3 and 1 reviews fewer than the sums of their months [measured].
- In all 7 cases the yearly list kept the later review of a pull request reviewed in two months. One case is kamilsk/dotfiles#788: the reviews of 2025-08-08T19:33:36Z (`PRR_kwDOCTsueM645EmP`) and 2025-09-13T08:52:07Z (`PRR_kwDOCTsueM6_7WbY`); 2025 keeps September 13 only [measured].
- The profile's view of a year counts the same way: a rebuild with this rule matches it on every day [measured].
- The profile's default view is the rolling last twelve months, so its range, and with it this rule, differs from a calendar year [inferred, not measured].

## The lists of a collection

```graphql
contributionsCollection(from: $from, to: $to) {
  restrictedContributionsCount
  totalCommitContributions totalIssueContributions totalPullRequestContributions
  totalPullRequestReviewContributions totalRepositoryContributions
  commitContributionsByRepository(maxRepositories: 100) {
    repository { nameWithOwner }
    contributions(first: 100) { totalCount pageInfo { hasNextPage } nodes { occurredAt commitCount } }
  }
  pullRequestReviewContributions(first: 100, after: $after) {
    totalCount pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }
    nodes { occurredAt pullRequest { id } pullRequestReview { id } }
  }
  issueContributions(first: 100) { totalCount nodes { occurredAt } }
  pullRequestContributions(first: 100) { totalCount nodes { occurredAt } }
  repositoryContributions(first: 100) { totalCount nodes { occurredAt } }
}
```

- **Commits come per repository and day,** not per commit. `occurredAt` is that day at 07:00Z/08:00Z. At most 100 repositories, with no paging over them. A repository's days are paged, so a month fits on one page [measured].
- **The lists are paged by 100 and come newest first.** Every list needs paging: in some months of 2026, kamilsk opened more than 100 issues [measured].
- **The totals are scalars** for the whole range. The calendar total adds what has no events.
- **There is no list of discussions,** nor of forks, although the reference counts forking always [S2]. kamilsk's days match without them [measured]. For others, this was not verified.
- **A visible review can be missing from the list.** The review `PRR_kwDOAJshA85kxCXa` on mitchellh/mapstructure#291 (submitted 2023-10-21T19:17:07Z) is returned by `pullRequest.reviews`. It is absent from the complete list of the 60 review contributions of 2023-10-19..23. The profile counts it: 25 against 24 on October 21, and the private parts agree at 18 [Codex]. An earlier review of the same pull request (May 2022) is listed.
- **The HTML activity summaries are not the calendar cells.** July 1, 2023 adds up to 16 in the activity and is 15 in the cell [Codex].

## Contributions without events

- `restrictedContributionsCount` counts contributions in repositories the token cannot read. The calendar puts them on days, but no list has their events [measured]. For kamilsk, 50 of the 54 contributions of 2013 (30 of them in December) and 57 in 2023 are restricted.
- Apart from them, the calendar total of a range can exceed its events: 1 in 2022, 3 in 2023 [measured]. One of them is the missing mapstructure review above. The rest is unexplained.
- The profile total can differ from the API total too: 7925 against 7921 in 2023 [Codex]. For other users the gap is larger with `restricted = 0`: thockin 1794 (API) against 1847 (profile) and BurntSushi 1837 against 1934 in 2025 [research run, re-measured 2026-10-31]. So exact reproduction is proven for kamilsk only.

## Timings

- One `contributionCalendar` request for a year takes 0.5–1.6 s. `lookup` before MAIN-159 took 0.7 s [measured].
- The events of a year take 4–9 s as parallel monthly requests (8 in flight), and 6–15 s in maintainer with 4 in flight. The heaviest year was 2023, with 3907 reviews.
- 12 months aliased into one request took longer than separate parallel requests: 9.4 s for the first round of 2023, then 4 more rounds for pages, 23 s in all [measured].
- The calendar totals of 12 months in one aliased request take 0.6–2.0 s. The scalar totals take 2.6–3.3 s [measured].
- maintainer with a warm cache takes 0.7–1.0 s [measured].

## How maintainer uses this

Since MAIN-159, `internal/service/github/contribution.go` and `contribution_cache.go`:

1. **Requests.** For every year of the scope, one aliased request asks for the calendar totals of each month, cut at now in the current year, and of the day before the year and the day after it.
2. **Cache.** A month is fetched again only if it is not cached or its total changed. The cache is `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/maintainer/contributions/<login>/<year>.json` (`~/.cache` without it), format version 1, written atomically. A broken cache is no cache.
3. **Fetching a month.** It takes the commits by repository and the four lists, all pages, and fails if a list ends before its `totalCount`, the commits add up to less than their total (more than 100 repositories), or a date is out of range.
4. **Months with undated contributions.** If the events date fewer contributions than the total, the month takes the days of the API calendar, and the command prints `warn:` when that month has reviews. The current month's calendar is not cached, because its lists may lag behind its total.
5. **Placing the events.** Reviews go on the UTC date, the latest per pull request in the year; commits on their day; issues, PRs and repositories on the UTC date. An event of a day outside the year belongs to the neighbour.
6. **Limits.** At most 4 GraphQL requests are in flight. `suggest` prints its moment in UTC (`Z`), so `git commit --date` keeps the day in any zone.

Rejected options:

- **Parsing the HTML as the source.** The owner rejected it; it depends on markup and private-count visibility. [MAIN-126](../issues/MAIN-126.md) moved away from it.
- **Only adding `Time-Zone: UTC`.** It proved unreliable [Codex].
- **Inferring the account's zone from the calendar residuals.** Offsets inferred month by month jumped from −4:15 to +9:00, and 52–59 days were off in 2022–2023 [measured].
- **A token without a zone.** Unproven, and impractical for a CLI.

## Reproduce

Profile days of a year:

```sh
curl -fsS "https://github.com/users/kamilsk/contributions?from=2025-01-01&to=2025-12-31" | python3 -c '
import re, sys; s = sys.stdin.read()
ids = dict(re.findall(r"data-date=\"(\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d)\" id=\"([^\"]+)\"", s))
tips = dict(re.findall(r"<tool-tip[^>]*for=\"([^\"]+)\"[^>]*>([^<]*)</tool-tip>", s))
for d, i in sorted(ids.items()): print(d, tips[i].split(" ")[0].replace("No", "0"))'
```

The GraphQL calendar of the same days. `gh` adds your local `Time-Zone`; pass `-H 'Time-Zone: UTC'` to compare, or use curl without it:

```sh
gh api graphql -f query='{ user(login: "kamilsk") { contributionsCollection(from: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z", to: "2025-01-07T23:59:59Z") {
  contributionCalendar { weeks { contributionDays { date contributionCount } } }
  pullRequestReviewContributions(first: 100) { nodes { occurredAt pullRequest { id } } } } } }'
```

The reviews of one pull request, to check the per-PR rule:

```sh
gh api graphql -f query='{ repository(owner: "kamilsk", name: "dotfiles") { pullRequest(number: 788) {
  reviews(first: 20, author: "kamilsk") { nodes { id state submittedAt } } } } }'
```

To check a whole year of maintainer against the profile, day by day, run `maintainer github contribution snapshot 2026 > 2026.json` and then `node .github/scripts/contribution-profile-diff.mjs kamilsk 2026.json`: it lists each day that differs and exits with 1 if there is one.

## What is left

- **Ranges depend on the request's zone.** If GitHub resolved two collections of one run in different zones, as Codex saw for the calendar aggregates, a month boundary could lose or repeat events. The lists were stable in 15 of 15 requests on 2026-10-31. The hardening is [MAIN-160](../issues/MAIN-160.md): overlap the monthly collections and count an event they share once.
- **An issue opened in the browser near local midnight** keeps the browser's date, but the API gives only the UTC moment. maintainer may put it one day off; none has been seen since 2022.
- **A pull request reviewed in a month that takes the calendar and again in another month** counts twice in maintainer's year. The calendar of a year would count it once.
- **The cache misses a change that keeps the total,** for example one contribution removed and another added in the same month.
- **Unexplained:** the gaps of thockin and BurntSushi, the mapstructure review missing from the list, the 3 extra contributions of 2023 in the calendar, and the cause of the alternation. GitHub has not been asked. On 2026-10-30, the owner decided to keep the drafted report local.
- **Unmeasured:** a token without a user zone; the rolling view of the profile; repository forks and discussions for an account that has them.
